correctness.rationale: The normal-basis expansion converts B v^[2]=v into B^m u=u over F2 without requiring invertibility. With B=S+S^-1 the relevant cyclic module map is multiplication by X^-m P_m, whose kernel dimension is deg gcd(X^n-1,P_m). Since P_m=P_r^(2^s), P_r(0)=1 and P_r prime-derivative X^(r-1) for odd r, P_r is squarefree and its X-class has finite odd order o_r; multiplicity in X^n-1 yields saturation iff 2^s o_r divides n. Taking large multiples proves least period. Independent GF2 matrix-vs-gcd comparison covered 225 pairs, plus F4 direct enumeration for n=3..6. These finite checks are corroboration, not proof.
